entries.title: Dataset of Generative AI Workload Power Profiles — measured Kestrel workload traces
entries.publisher: National Laboratory of the Rockies / Open Energy Data Initiative
entries.physical_boundary: Kestrel GPU/HPC workload power measurement; exact sub-channel reference plane to be confirmed from archive metadata
entries.access_method: Public archive download; approximately 1,021.3 MB, not downloaded in this increment
notes: Catalogue version 2 is listed as updated 17 July 2026.
Dataset includes 5 Hz and 10 Hz time-series profiles; the conservative maximum interval is recorded as 200 ms.
The dataset also contains model-generated whole-facility profiles; those are registered separately as modelled evidence.
The exact README, columns, units, time basis, instrument bandwidth and anti-alias response have not yet been inspected.

entries.title: High-resolution AI Data Center Training Workloads — multi-GPU node sessions
entries.physical_boundary: Eight-GPU H100/B200 node telemetry: power, utilization, memory, GPU temperature and workload session metadata
entries.access_method: Public GitHub repository and figshare DOI 10.6084/m9.figshare.31654879
notes: 32 H100/B200 eight-GPU node training sessions are described.
Nominal node monitoring interval is 20 ms (50 Hz); conservative Nyquist is 25 Hz.
The dataset README states CC BY-NC-ND 4.0. No Luminous commercial use or redistribution of adapted data without separate rights-holder permission.
Instrument analogue bandwidth and anti-alias response are not specified by the paper.

entries.title: ELF: The Energy-Latency Frontier dataset for GPU inference
entries.physical_boundary: GPU board power, achieved throughput and four-phase inference latency on NVIDIA T4/L4/A10G/A100 platforms
notes: 20 inference models are reported across four GPU platforms.
Board power-limit sweeps and graphics-clock/DVFS sweeps are included.
A high-rate power-cap actuation trace is described, but the actual sample interval, sensor bandwidth and anti-alias response have not been verified; it is not registered as fast-transient evidence.
NLM catalogue describes the headline artifact data/elf_master.csv with 2,636 settled operating-point rows; the companion data/elf_master_dictionary.md documents columns.
The sweep collections contain 6,488 measured windows, typically two to three consecutive two-second windows per operating point.

The first window after a power-cap change contains a settling pause in NVML's trailing power average; the paper's analysis discards it for settled comparisons, while the source files retain all windows.

The separate high-rate power-cap actuation trace remains unprofiled: exact sample interval, analog sensor bandwidth, timestamp jitter and anti-alias response are unknown. It is not eligible for fast transient claims.
entries.citation: Apartsin, A. and Aperstein, Y. (2026), ELF: The Energy-Latency Frontier dataset for GPU inference, Zenodo, DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23074732.
required_notices: Provide CC BY 4.0 attribution and mark changes.
The high-rate power-cap trace cannot be used for a fast transient claim until its measurement metadata are inspected.

entries.title: Frontier Job-Centric Telemetry Dataset
entries.physical_boundary: Frontier scheduler-job-linked node and processor power, thermal and performance telemetry
entries.access_method: Globus access route; local access grant and terms not verified
notes: 152,400 jobs are described across selected days in 2024 and 2025.
Catalogue size is approximately 470.41 GB and 1,182,147 files.
The public catalogue does not establish a reuse or redistribution licence in the reviewed metadata; all licence permissions remain unknown.
Sampling interval and sensor bandwidth are not stated in the reviewed dataset catalogue.
entries.citation: Huk, L., Palumbo, R., Adamson, R., Osborne, T. and Lester, C. (2026), Frontier Job-Centric Telemetry Dataset, ORNL, DOI: 10.13139/OLCF/3013979.
required_notices: Do not download or redistribute until access and licence terms are confirmed.
Globus availability does not imply commercial-use or redistribution permission.

entries.title: LLM-PowerTrace: A Dataset of Time-Resolved GPU Power Traces for AI Compute
entries.physical_boundary: Per-GPU power traces and workload/request execution metadata as described in preprint; raw dataset release not verified
entries.access_method: Preprint and cited project explorer; complete dataset release described as upon acceptance
notes: The preprint reports 1,788 fine-tuning runs and 405 serving runs.
Nominal telemetry interval is 100 ms; this is 10 Hz sampling with 5 Hz Nyquist, not a VRM transient measurement.
The preprint's licence does not by itself establish the dataset's separate reuse licence.
Dataset access, complete release status and dataset licence must be rechecked before use.
entries.citation: Wang et al. (2026), LLM-PowerTrace: A Dataset of Time-Resolved GPU Power Traces for AI Compute, arXiv:2610.38315.
required_notices: Do not treat the complete corpus as available until the stated release gate is confirmed.
Do not infer dataset licensing from the preprint licence.

entries.title: Data Center Flexibility Dataset — Argonne JLSE project
entries.publisher: Argonne National Laboratory / Joint Laboratory for System Evaluation
entries.physical_boundary: Planned B200/H100 inference workload telemetry with node GPU/CPU/DRAM power and per-request QoS
entries.access_method: Research project description only; no downloadable public dataset verified
notes: Planned sweeps include GPU clock, GPU/CPU power caps, batch size and request concurrency.
Planned QoS channels include time-to-first-token, latency and tokens per second.
Keep as a watchlist item, not a usable dataset.
entries.citation: Argonne National Laboratory, Data Center Flexibility Dataset project page, accessed 10 November 2026.
required_notices: This is a planned research data product, not a downloadable corpus.
